attributes.title: Enter
attributes.sample:
{{! Every notice is keyed, so replaying swaps IDENTITIES — the old ones
    exit while the new ones enter, rather than one list mutating in place }}
<Presence @items={{this.items}} @key={{keyOf}} @mode='popLayout' as |note h|>
  {{! initial is the pose painted BEFORE the first frame; animate is home.
      The transition is PER VALUE: opacity is a short tween because a fade
      reads as instant anyway, while scale and y are springs so the card
      arrives with weight. One blanket duration would flatten both. }}
  <article
    {{motion
      presence=h
      initial=(to opacity=0 scale=0.55 y=56)
      animate=(to opacity=1 scale=1 y=0)
      exit=(to opacity=0 scale=0.9 y=-20)
      transition=(perValue
        opacity=(tween duration=0.16)
        scale=(spring bounce=0.48 visualDuration=0.42)
        y=(spring bounce=0.38 visualDuration=0.42)
      )
    }}
  >{{note.title}}</article>
</Presence>

lesson.concept: Arrival can use different property responses
lesson.why: The notice has explicit initial and target values. Scale and vertical movement use springs while opacity uses a short tween, and a second arrival can be offset without duplicating the component.
lesson.experiment: Compare Jack in the box and Polite entrance. Follow the text baseline and the opacity separately during the first appearance.
lesson.pitfall: Binding a style attribute on the same element can overwrite Motion's transform during a Glimmer update.
lesson.combine: Combine with presence when the same notice also needs a retained exit.
